correctness.rationale: Every disjoint trap forces \(0<u<1\) and \(p_\varepsilon(u)\le0\); the exact critical factorization \((u-u_c)^2H(u)\) with \(H(u)>0\) on \([0,1]\), together with monotonicity in \(\varepsilon\), excludes all such traps above \(\varepsilon_c\) through \(1/20\). Strict sign and convexity yield two exact-image pairs below threshold. The lower pair is the smallest closed invariant reachable pair containing 0 and 1. Nondegenerate Taylor expansion proves the square-root collision and a reciprocal-increment argument proves \(1/m\) critical boundary decay. Source code independently checked 2232 finite diagnostics, not substituted for the proof.

value.rationale: The maximum noise permitting robust preservation of the two alternating reachable components is a natural exact resilience invariant for a superstable quadratic cycle. The sharp threshold is an algebraic constant and the fold is reached while the spatial gap is still >0.58, demonstrating loss of robust band separation without a band collision. The globally necessary endpoint inequality and one-sided critical slowing are a substantive, reproducible finite-dimensional dynamical benchmark, not merely a numerical tangency estimate.
